name: Acetic acid (methanol carbonylation)
principle: Methanol reacts with carbon monoxide in the presence of an iodide promoter and a rhodium (Monsanto) or iridium (Cativa) catalyst. Iridium lets the reaction run with less water, which needs fewer drying columns, gives fewer by-products such as propionic acid and suppresses the water-gas shift. The two processes can share the same plant.
advantages: Less water and fewer by-products than rhodium (Wikipedia)
limitations: Source gives no yields or conditions
